target_customer: B2B SaaS and data product companies whose enterprise customers want the vendor's data delivered to their own data warehouse
problem: Customers of SaaS vendors increasingly ask for raw data in Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift or Databricks, and each vendor would otherwise build and maintain a separate pipeline per warehouse.
business_model: Usage based API and platform, priced per destination rather than per row, with cloud and self hosted deployment
product_category: Data warehouse integration and data sharing infrastructure for SaaS vendors

founders.name: Charles Chretien
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and author of the company's seed announcement. No opened source gives education or prior employers.

founders.name: Conor McCarter
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. No opened source gives background.

competitors.name: Snowflake Secure Data Sharing
competitors.what: Native in warehouse sharing that lets a vendor share live data with customers on Snowflake without copying
competitors.traction_then: Documented and used by SaaS vendors by early 2020; limited to customers on Snowflake

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable multi tenant sync to several warehouse dialects with schema handling, security and scale. Standard data engineering, with the hard parts being many destinations and enterprise security.

defensibility.rationale: Once a vendor ships exports to customers on Prequel, switching means re-onboarding every customer destination. Warehouse vendors and large SaaS companies could build equivalents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Prequel. Sacra notes large SaaS platforms increasingly build native exports, which is a continuing pressure.

market_need_then: Warehouse centric data stacks were spreading by 2020 and 2021, and a Snowflake guide for SaaS providers says customers increasingly ask vendors to share raw data back with them.

branding.domain_note: Company site is prequel.co; no purchase history found.

identity.logo: not described by an opened source
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct and benefit led; short headlines and customer proof (from the company site).

brand_strength.rationale: A B2B infrastructure brand known through named customer logos on its site. No press about the brand itself, mascot or community. The word Prequel is shared with a film term and at least one unrelated startup, so search results are crowded.

outcome_analysis: Prequel is active and, by its own seed announcement, signed customers including LogRocket, Metronome, Modern Treasury and Postscript, with synced destinations growing over 35 percent monthly in 2023. It raised a 5.2M seed in September 2023, more than two years after the batch, so early capital efficiency mattered. The product rides the shift to warehouse centric data stacks, while native exports from large vendors are the main threat.
notes: The 5.2M seed is stated in the company's own announcement dated 2023-09-26 and appears in search listings of NextView and Stage 2 Capital pages (not opened). A Work-Bench led 3.3M seed in December 2024 belongs to a different company also named Prequel (application reliability) and is excluded. Founder education and employers appear only on secondary profile sites that were not opened, so they are left null. Fivetran is named only as an ETL partner in an undated guide, so it is not listed as a competitor. Prequel's own blog post introducing the product is dated 2022-05, a year after the batch.
